ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
During the ripening process of banana fruit, the stored substances in the fruit are continuously metabolized and transformed, and the banana gradually becomes sweeter. In Figure A, curves I and II respectively indicate the changing trends of the contents of two substances during the ripening process of banana fruit. Please answer:
Take equal amounts of banana pulp ripened to day X and day Y, and add equal amounts of distilled water respectively to make extracts. Then add 5 mL of the extract from day X to each of test tubes a and b, and add 5 mL of the extract from day Y to each of test tubes c and d, as shown in Figure B. Add equal amounts of Fehling's reagent to each of test tubes b and d, and after boiling, tube b is brick-red. What is the substance being tested in the two tubes?

In Figure A, curves I and II respectively indicate the changing trends of the contents of two substances during the ripening process of banana fruit. Please answer: Take equal amounts of banana pulp ripened to day X and day Y, and add equal amounts of distilled water respectively to make extracts. Then add 5 mL of the extract from day X to each of test tubes a and b, and add 5 mL of the extract from day Y to each of test tubes c and d, as shown in Figure B. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in Figure A there are two curves changing with ripening time; curve I decreases with time, and curve II increases with time; in Figure B, test tubes a and b are added with the banana extract from day X, and test tubes c and d are added with the banana extract from day Y, among which test tubes b and d are also added with Fehling's reagent and boiled. Then reason: Fehling's reagent is used under heating conditions to test for reducing sugar; if reducing sugar is present, a brick-red precipitate will appear. The stem states that tube b is brick-red, therefore the substance being tested in tubes b and d is reducing sugar.
